blocks.html:
• Module: Packages/Infrastructure/Sources/Infrastructure/UploadKit — standalone, uses nothing else from SiteLog (D02)

Goal: move 150–250 files and several GB to R2, surviving network loss, suspension, termination, reboot and presigned-URL expiry.

04.1 Boundary

  • In: a file URL, metadata, an endpoint, an injected store. Does not import DomainLayer.
swift
public protocol UploadStore: Sendable {
    func upsert(_ job: UploadJobRecord) async throws
    func job(id: UploadJobID) async throws -> UploadJobRecord?
    func job(forTaskDescription key: String) async throws -> UploadJobRecord?
    func pendingJobs(limit: Int) async throws -> [UploadJobRecord]
    func updatePart(_ part: UploadPartRecord) async throws
    func delete(id: UploadJobID) async throws
}
  • The app implements it over SwiftData in Persistence.
  • UploadKit ships InMemoryUploadStore: the state machine is testable with no app, DB or network.
  • Files: UploadCoordinator (actor, entry point), UploadStateMachine (pure), ChunkPlanner, PresignedURLProvider, BackgroundSessionDelegate.

04.2 Protocol

  • The backend never touches bytes. Endpoints: 03-backend.md §3.
StepCallReturns
1POST /uploads {key, byteSize, contentType, sha256}single {uploadId, url} or multipart {uploadId, partSizeBytes, parts[]}
2PUT <presigned url> (part temp file)200 + ETag
3POST /uploads/:id/complete {parts[{number, etag}]}{remoteKey, verificationCode, verified} — idempotent
4POST /uploads/:id/parts/refresh {numbers}Fresh URLs — mandatory after a long kill
5DELETE /uploads/:idAbort
  • Mode from byteSize: under 5 MB single PUT, else multipart with uniform 8 MB parts (R2 requires equal non-final parts, so ChunkPlanner splits by fixed size).
  • Every call carries a Firebase ID token; the key prefix must match its uid.

04.3 iOS background constraints

ConstraintConsequence
Background sessions accept only uploadTask(with:fromFile:)Each part written to a temp file; at most maxMaterializedPartsPerJob ahead; deleted on 200 + ETag
Tasks created while backgrounded are discretionaryEnqueue the first batch in the foreground; say "will upload when idle"
taskIdentifier is reusedKey on taskDescription = "jobID#part"
Nothing survives termination in RAMRecreate the session with the same identifier and reconcile
  • Session: isDiscretionary = false, sessionSendsLaunchEvents = true, resource timeout 7 days, handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession wired in the app delegate.

Cold-launch reconciliation (the usual cause of "stuck at 60%"):

TaskRecordAction
AliveExistsReattach
AliveMissingCancel and log
MissinguploadingReset to pending
  • A realtime snapshot adds server state; jobs only move forward.

04.4 State machine

pending → planning → uploading ⇄ waitingForURL / waitingForNetwork → completing → synced
                         └────────────► failed (retry budget exhausted only)
swift
public struct UploadStateMachine {
    public enum Event { case planned([UploadPartRecord]), partSucceeded(Int, etag: String),
        partFailed(Int, FailureReason), urlsRefreshed([UploadPartRecord]),
        networkBecameAvailable, completed(remoteKey: String), cancelledByUser }
    public enum Effect { case enqueuePart(Int), refreshURLs([Int]), callComplete([Int: String]),
        scheduleRetry(Int, after: TimeInterval), deleteTempFile(Int), abort(FailureReason) }
    public func reduce(state: UploadJobState, event: Event) -> (UploadJobState, [Effect])
}
  • reduce is deterministic, no I/O; UploadCoordinator is the only executor of effects.
CauseReasonHandling
401/403 on a presigned URL.urlExpiredwaitingForURL, no budget consumed
Not connected.offlinewaitingForNetwork, no budget consumed
5xx, timeout, 429 (Retry-After).serverTransient / .timeoutRetry, budget consumed
400, 404, 411, 413.permanentAbort — the backend never returns these for retryable cases
ETag or checksum mismatch.integrityAbort, flag for the user
  • Retry: delay = min(2s × 2^attempt, 300s) × jitter(0.8…1.2), max 5 attempts.
  • Jitter is mandatory: 200 files failing at one signal loss must not retry together.

04.5 Policy

PolicyDetail
Priority queueHost-supplied priority (03); plans low; stamped derivatives never upload
WiFi-onlyallowsCellularAccess = false, on by default
DedupeSame sha256 in a project → skip, reuse the existing remoteKey
Concurrency3 jobs, 4 connections per host — more times out together on weak networks
Local filesNever auto-deleted; cleanup is user-initiated and synced-only (09)
Logging{jobID, part n/N, bytes, elapsedMs, attempt, status, reason}; never presigned URLs
swift
public enum UploadConstants {
    public static let partSizeBytes: Int = 8 * 1024 * 1024
    public static let singlePutThresholdBytes: Int = 5 * 1024 * 1024
    public static let maxConcurrentJobs: Int = 3
    public static let maxConnectionsPerHost: Int = 4
    public static let maxMaterializedPartsPerJob: Int = 2
    public static let minFreeDiskBytes: Int64 = 500 * 1024 * 1024
    public static let resourceTimeout: TimeInterval = 604_800
    public static let retryBaseDelay: TimeInterval = 2
    public static let retryCapDelay: TimeInterval = 300
    public static let maxRetryAttempts: Int = 5
    public static let sessionIdentifier: String = "app.dd.site.log.upload.background"
}
RiskHandling
Orphaned parts after abortDELETE /uploads/:id + 7-day bucket lifecycle rule
Disk fillsStop planning new jobs, keep running ones, show numbers
Account switch with pending jobsCancel old uid's jobs, delete temp files, never write into the new prefix
Clock skew vs expiresAt403 is the truth; expiresAt only drives proactive refresh

Done

  • 200 files / 2 GB complete with matching server hashes
  • Kill mid-transfer resumes without re-uploading parts
  • Airplane mode → waitingForNetwork with budget intact
  • 60 s URL TTL refreshes automatically
  • WiFi-only on cellular sends zero bytes

Tests

  • Full (state × event) matrix
  • Final part failure never calls complete
  • Budget rules
  • Exhausted budget keeps the original
  • Backoff with stubbed RNG
  • ChunkPlanner sizes
  • Single-PUT threshold
  • Dedupe
  • All three reconciliation cases
  • Priority order
  • MockTransport flow with 503 at part 3
  • Real kill on device

• Modules: SiteLog/Presentation/Sync, DataLayer (sync engine), Packages/Infrastructure/Sources/Infrastructure/Networking (D03)

Goal: sign in once, work fully offline, sync all metadata across devices over a hand-written delta protocol.

  • Firebase is identity and crash reporting only; all data is in Postgres.
InOut
Firebase Auth (Sign in with Apple, email)Firestore, in any role
Cursor-based delta pull, batched push, tombstones, LWWMulti-user sharing, real-time co-editing, SSO
Offline mutation queue in SwiftDataMedia in the sync protocol — bytes go to R2
Account deletion
  • Without Firestore, three things are ours: offline persistence (SwiftData mutation queue), delete propagation (tombstones), listener fan-out (pg_notify).
  • Remote media: a pulled Capture carries its object key → presigned GET → shown with Kingfisher (downsampled, disk-cached, cache key without the query string). Local originals always read from disk (D05).

08.1 Offline-first and auth

  • Local is the source of truth while recording; the server once synced. Writes land in SwiftData and return immediately; no screen waits on the network.
  • Launching offline after a prior sign-in goes straight in.
  • getIDToken(forcingRefresh: false) on every request — never hand-cache it. The backend verifies with checkRevoked: true; keys embed the uid ({uid}/{projectID}/…). One 401 interceptor refreshes; no retry budget consumed.

08.2 Protocol

POST /sync/pull  { since: <rev>, limit }        → { changes: {table: [rows]}, nextRev, hasMore }
POST /sync/push  { mutations: [{ table, id, op, clientUpdatedAt, fields }] }
                                                → { results: [{ id, status: applied|superseded, serverRow? }], serverRev }
  • Revisions, not timestamps: each row has a server-assigned rev from a per-user counter incremented in the write transaction, so it is gap-free and commit-ordered (03-backend.md §7).
  • Conflicts: captures, issue_captures insert-only (UUIDs cannot conflict); everything else LWW on clientUpdatedAt, tie-broken by id; checklist_results per (run, item); sessions.state monotonic (draft < active < closed < exported) so an offline device cannot reopen a signed report.
  • Deletes are soft (deleted_at + new rev); tombstones purge after 90 days; a cursor older than that gets { resyncRequired: true } and resyncs from 0.
  • The client queues mutations in dependency order (projects → locations → plan_sheets → sessions → captures → issues → issue_captures → annotations → checklist_*); the server applies a batch in one transaction with deferred constraints.

08.3 Client engine

swift
actor MetadataSyncEngine {          // Data/; triggered by use cases
    func sync() async throws        // pull, push, pull again if serverRev advanced
    func enqueue(_ mutation: Mutation) async
    func fullResync() async throws
}

enum SyncConstants {
    static let syncInterval: TimeInterval = 300
    static let pullPageSize: Int = 500
    static let pushBatchSize: Int = 200
    static let backoffBaseDelay: TimeInterval = 5
    static let backoffMaxDelay: TimeInterval = 600
    static let tombstoneRetentionDays: Int = 90
}
  • Triggers: foreground, network restored, every syncInterval, queue reaching pushBatchSize — never per write.
  • superseded is not a failure: adopt serverRow.
  • Every cycle logs {pulled, pushed, superseded, elapsedMs, cursor}.
  • Account deletion: in-app → reauthenticate → DELETE /account (server removes R2 objects and rows) → local store, Keychain, media; numbers shown first; final audit entry.
RiskHandling
Account switch with pending workCancel jobs, delete temp files, clear the queue
Cursor lostFull resync from rev 0
Clock skew picks the wrong LWW winnerAccepted for metadata; captures are immutable
Sign in with Apple hides the emailNothing depends on a real email

Done

  • Offline relaunch after sign-in
  • A project created offline on A appears on B within one interval
  • A delete on A stays deleted on B
  • B cannot un-export A's session
  • 80 generated locations sync as one batch
  • Resync from 0 reproduces the store
  • Token expiry mid-sync loses nothing

Tests

  • Monotonic state across 16 pairs
  • LWW tie-break
  • Tombstones never resurrect
  • Stale cursor → resync
  • Queue survives termination in order
  • superseded adoption
  • 200 mutations = one request
  • Account switch
  • 10 concurrent 401s → one refresh

blocks.html:
• Module: Packages/Infrastructure/Sources/Infrastructure/Realtime (D04)

Goal: learn what the server knows first — assembly done, hash checked, mismatch — without polling 243 jobs. An observation channel on URLSessionWebSocketTask; never controls UploadKit.

Boundary

  • Uploads work at 100% with the channel dead.
  • Neither folder uses the other; the app layer turns events into UploadStore operations.
  • Events may only advance a job; server silence never means "not done".
  • CI builds the app with Realtime removed.
DirectionMessages (line-delimited JSON)
Client → serverauth {token} · subscribe {sessionID} · ping {at}
Server → clientsnapshot {sessionID, completed[], failed[]} · jobCompleted {jobID, remoteKey, sha256} · jobFailed {jobID, reason} · pong {at}
  • snapshot is always first after subscribe — it is the recovery path, so delivery need not be guaranteed. Missed messages are never replayed.
  • The token goes in the first auth message, never the URL; no auth within authTimeout → closed; close code 4001 on expiry → refresh and reconnect.
  • Connect only when foregrounded, a job is unsynced and the network is allowed; disconnect on background.
  • Ping every pingInterval (cellular NAT drops silently); re-arm receive after every message (the classic silent bug); reconnect with its own backoff, unlimited.
  • jobCompleted is trusted only if its sha256 matches the local hash; otherwise it is an integrity failure. Unknown jobIDs are ignored; handling is idempotent.
swift
public enum RealtimeConstants {
    public static let pingInterval: TimeInterval = 30
    public static let pongTimeout: TimeInterval = 10
    public static let authTimeout: TimeInterval = 5
    public static let reconnectBaseDelay: TimeInterval = 1
    public static let reconnectMaxDelay: TimeInterval = 60
    public static let maxMessageBytes: Int = 64 * 1024   // larger closes without parsing
}

Done

  • 50 jobs reach synced via events
  • The same 50 with the flag off, only slower
  • A two-minute drop reconnects and the snapshot restores state
  • A wrong sha256 raises a flag instead of synced
  • Backgrounding closes within 1 s

Tests

  • Decode all types + malformed
  • Oversized message
  • Missing pong → backoff
  • Backoff cap and jitter
  • Hash mismatch
  • Applying one event 10× equals once
  • Snapshot applies forward only
  • Unknown jobID
  • Flow against a mock WebSocket server
